question:
Examine the system
$$kx+2y=3$$
$$2x+ky=3$$
for different real values of $k$.

(a) Determine the values of $k$ for which the system has a unique solution.

(b) Examine the system when $k=2$ and state the number of solutions.

(c) Examine the system when $k=-2$ and justify whether it is consistent.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient determinant is
$$D= egin{vmatrix}k & 2\2 & k\end{vmatrix}=k^2-4=(k-2)(k+2)$$
The system has a unique solution when $D eq0$. Therefore,
$$k eq2\quad ext{and}\quad k eq-2$$

(b)
When $k=2$, the equations become
$$2x+2y=3$$
$$2x+2y=3$$
The two equations are identical. Therefore, the system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions satisfying
$$x+y= rac{3}{2}$$

(c)
When $k=-2$, the equations become
$$-2x+2y=3$$
$$2x-2y=3$$
Multiplying the first equation by $-1$ gives
$$2x-2y=-3$$
This contradicts $2x-2y=3$. Therefore, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.A:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq2,-2$
(b) For $k=2$, infinitely many solutions satisfying $x+y=\frac{3}{2}$
(c) For $k=-2$, the system is inconsistent and has no solution
options.B:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq2$ only
(b) For $k=2$, there is a unique solution
(c) For $k=-2$, infinitely many solutions exist
options.C:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq-2$ only
(b) For $k=2$, the system is inconsistent
(c) For $k=-2$, the two equations are identical
options.D:
(a) Unique solution for every real $k$
(b) For $k=2$, $x=y=\frac34$ is the only solution
(c) For $k=-2$, $x=-\frac34,y=\frac34$ is the only solution
